href="#s55D8254CE4755B6393C0CE875105618D">103</a></div></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;height:20px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;height:20px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div><br/></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;"><br/></span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><a id="s6A06744F7093558CB36B0EA27FBDD87A"></a></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;" href="#s7A24416E6E325981B2DB78D6BBC49653"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</span></a></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:center;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">GLOSSARY OF OIL AND NATURAL GAS TERMS</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The following are abbreviations and definitions of certain terms used in this Annual Report on Form&#160;10-K, which are commonly used in the oil and natural gas industry:</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Bbl</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One stock tank barrel of 42 U.S. gallons liquid volume used herein in reference to crude oil, condensate or NGLs.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Bbl/d</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One Bbl per day.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Boe</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One barrel of oil equivalent, calculated by converting natural gas to oil equivalent barrels at a ratio of six Mcf of natural gas to one Bbl of oil. This is an energy content correlation and does not reflect a value or price relationship between the commodities.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Boe/d</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One Boe per day.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Btu</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One British thermal unit, which is the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of a one-pound mass of water by one-degree Fahrenheit.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Completion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. &#160;The&#160;process of preparing an oil and gas wellbore for production through the&#160;installation of permanent production equipment, as well as perforation and fracture stimulation to optimize production.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Development well</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. A well drilled within the proved area of an oil or natural gas reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be productive.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Differential</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. An adjustment to the price of oil or natural gas from an established spot market price to reflect differences in the quality and location of oil or natural gas.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Exploratory well</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. A well drilled to find a new field or to find a new reservoir in a field previously found to be productive of oil or natural gas in another reservoir.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Extension well.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;A well drilled to extend the limits of a known reservoir.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Field</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. An area consisting of a single reservoir or multiple reservoirs all grouped on, or related to, the same individual geological structural feature or stratigraphic condition. The field name refers to the surface area, although it may refer to both the surface and the underground productive formations. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Flush production. </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">First yield from a flowing well during its most productive period after it is first completed and put online.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Formation</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. A layer of rock which has distinct characteristics that differs from nearby rock.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Horizontal drilling</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. A drilling technique used in certain formations where a well is drilled vertically to a certain depth and then drilled at a right angle within a specified interval.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">LIBOR. </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">London Interbank Offered Rate. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">MBbl</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One thousand barrels of crude oil, condensate or NGLs.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">MBoe</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One thousand Boe.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Mcf</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One thousand cubic feet of natural gas.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Mcf/d</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One Mcf per day.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">MMBtu</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One million British thermal units.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">MMcf</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. One million cubic feet of natural gas.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">NGL.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> Natural gas liquids. These are naturally occurring substances found in natural gas, including ethane, butane, isobutane, propane and natural gasoline, that can be collectively removed from produced natural gas, separated in these substances and sold. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">NYMEX</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The New York Mercantile Exchange.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Operator</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The individual or company responsible for the development and/or production of an oil or natural gas well or lease.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Proved developed reserves</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. Reserves that can be expected to be recovered through existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods or in which the cost of the required equipment is relatively minor compared with the cost of a new well.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Proved reserves</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The estimated quantities of oil, NGLs and natural gas that geological and engineering data demonstrate with reasonable certainty to be commercially recoverable in future years from known reservoirs under existing economic and operating conditions.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Proved undeveloped reserves&#160;or PUD</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">.&#160;Proved reserves that are expected to be recovered from new wells on undrilled acreage, or from existing wells where a relatively major expenditure is required for completion or recompletion.&#160;</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">3</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;" href="#s7A24416E6E325981B2DB78D6BBC49653"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</span></a></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Realized price</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The cash market price less differentials.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Recompletion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The completion for production of an existing wellbore in another formation from that which the well has been previously completed.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Reserves</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. Estimated remaining quantities of oil and natural gas and related substances anticipated to be economically producible, as of a given date, by application of development projects to known accumulations. In addition, there must exist, or there must be a reasonable expectation that there will exist, the legal right to produce or a revenue interest in the production, installed means of delivering oil and natural gas or related substances to market and all permits and financing required to implement the project. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Reservoir</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. A porous and permeable underground formation containing a natural accumulation of producible oil and/or natural gas that is confined by impermeable rock or water barriers and is individual and separate from other reservoirs.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Royalty interest.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;An interest in an oil or gas property entitling the owner to shares of the production free of costs of exploration, development and production operations.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Spot market price</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The cash market price without reduction for expected quality, location, transportation and demand adjustments.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Wellbore</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The hole drilled by a drill bit that is equipped for oil and natural gas production once the well has been completed. Also called well or borehole.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Working interest</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The interest in an oil and gas property (typically a leasehold interest) that gives the owner the right to drill, produce and conduct operations on the property and&#160;to a share of production, subject to all royalties and other burdens and to all costs of exploration, development and operations and all risks in connection therewith.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Workover.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;Operations on a producing well to restore or increase production.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">WTI</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. West Texas Intermediate is a grade of crude oil used as a benchmark in oil pricing.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">4</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><a id="s9D8A23FC829C5A328EABD04C0C0F4042"></a></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><a style="line-height:174%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:center;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">GLOSSARY OF CERTAIN OTHER TERMS</span></div><div style="line-height:174%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The following are definitions of certain other terms that are used in this Annual Report:</span></div><div contemplated by the Contribution Agreement.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span the outstanding membership interests in CRP to the Company in connection with the Business Combination. As of December 31, 2019, the Centennial Contributors&#8217; ownership interest in CRP was approximately 0.4%. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">The Company, We, Our or Us. </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">(i)&#160;Centennial Resource Development,&#160;Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries including CRP, following the closing of the Business Combination and (ii)&#160;Silver Run Acquisition Corporation prior to the closing of the Business Combination.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Class&#160;A Common Stock.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> Our Class&#160;A Common Stock, par value $0.0001 per share.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Class&#160;C Common Stock.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> Our Class&#160;C Common Stock, par value $0.0001 per share, which was issued to the Centennial Contributors in connection with the Business Combination.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Contribution Agreement</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The Contribution Agreement, dated as of July&#160;6, 2016, among the Centennial Contributors, CRP and NewCo, as amended by Amendment No.&#160;1 thereto, dated as of July&#160;29, 2016, and the Joinder Agreement, dated as of October&#160;7, 2016, by the Company.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">CRP</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. Centennial Resource Production,&#160;LLC, a Delaware limited liability company.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">CRP Common Units</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. The units representing common membership interests in CRP.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">GMT Acquisition.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> The acquisition of certain undeveloped acreage and producing oil and natural gas properties of GMT Exploration Company LLC, which closed on June 8, 2017.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">IPO</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. Risk Factors </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">in this Annual Report.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Reserve engineering is a process of estimating underground accumulations of oil and natural gas that cannot be measured in an exact way. In addition, the results of drilling, testing and production activities may justify revisions of estimates that were made previously. If significant, such revisions would change the schedule of any further production and development drilling. Accordingly, reserve estimates may differ significantly from the quantities of oil and natural gas that are ultimately recovered.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Should one or more of the risks or uncertainties described in this Annual Report occur, or should underlying assumptions prove incorrect, our actual results and plans could differ materially from those expressed in any forward-looking statements.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">6</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;" href="#s7A24416E6E325981B2DB78D6BBC49653"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</span></a></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">All forward-looking statements, expressed or implied, included in this Annual Report are expressly qualified in their entirety by this cautionary statement. BUSINESS AND PROPERTIES</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Overview</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Centennial Resource Development, Inc. is an independent oil and natural gas company focused on the development of unconventional oil and associated liquids-rich natural gas reserves in the Permian Basin. Throughout this Annual Report, unless the context otherwise indicates, references to the &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;Centennial,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us,&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221; refer to Centennial Resource Development, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiary, Centennial Resource Production, LLC (&#8220;CRP&#8221;).</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Our principal business objective is to increase shareholder value by building a premier development company focused on horizontal drilling in the Delaware Basin. We intend to grow our production and oil and natural gas reserves by developing our acreage with an increased focus on optimizing drilling and completion results, drilling extended laterals and managing costs, with an overall objective of improving our rates of return on all wells drilled and thereby funding our drilling and development capex entirely from cash flows from operations. We also intend to grow production and reserves through selective acquisitions that meet our strategic and financial objectives. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Organizational Structure</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:4px;padding-top:4px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">On October&#160;11, 2016, the acquisition of approximately&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">89%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;of the outstanding membership interests in CRP was consummated (the &#8220;Business Combination&#8221;). We currently own an approximate </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">99.6%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> membership interest in CRP due to various equity transactions. </span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span As a result, we are able to efficiently develop our drilling inventory and focus on maximizing returns to our stakeholders. We have established commercial production on our acreage using horizontal drilling from nine distinct zones: the Avalon Shale, 1st Bone Spring Sand, 2nd&#160;Bone Spring Sand, 2nd Bone Spring Shale, 3rd&#160;Bone Spring Sand, 3rd Bone Spring Shale, Upper Wolfcamp&#160;A, Lower Wolfcamp&#160;A, Wolfcamp&#160;B and Wolfcamp&#160;C. We operated, a six-rig drilling program through mid-September 2019 and a five-rig program thereafter, which enabled us to complete and bring online </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">84</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;gross operated wells during the year. Approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">76%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> of our total acreage is located in Texas, primarily Reeves County, in the southern portion of the Delaware Basin and the remaining </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">24%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> is located in New Mexico, in Lea County, in the northern portion of the Delaware Basin. The relatively high proportion of our operated acreage that is held by production gives us significant operational control and capital spending flexibility. This allows us to execute our development program with significant control over the timing and allocation of capital expenditures and application of the optimal drilling and completion techniques to efficiently develop our resource base. Our development drilling plan is comprised exclusively of horizontal drilling with an ongoing focus on optimizing completions, improving drilling results and managing costs.</span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">10</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><a id="s39B3B424979B541E83E09E2EC726B981"></a></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;" href="#s7A24416E6E325981B2DB78D6BBC49653"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</span></a></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Proved Oil and Gas Reserves</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Reserve estimates are inherently imprecise, and estimates for new discoveries and undeveloped locations are more imprecise than reserve estimates for producing oil and gas properties. style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;">Total proved pre-tax PV 10% (&#8220;Pre-tax PV 10%&#8221;) may be considered a non-GAAP financial measure as defined by the SEC and is derived from the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows (the &#8216;&#8216;Standardized Measure&#8217;&#8217;), which is the most directly comparable U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) financial measure. Pre-tax PV 10% is computed on the same basis as the Standardized Measure but without deducting future income taxes. We believe Pre-tax PV 10% is a useful measure for investors when evaluating the relative monetary significance of our oil and natural gas properties. We further believe investors may utilize our Pre-tax PV 10% as a basis for comparison of the relative size and value of our proved reserves to other companies because many factors that are unique to each individual company impact the amount of future income taxes to be paid. Our management uses this measure when assessing the potential return on investment related to our oil and gas properties and acquisitions. However, Pre-tax PV 10% is not a substitute for the Standardized Measure. Our Pre-tax PV 10% and Standardized Measure do not purport to present the fair value of our proved oil, NGL and natural gas reserves.</span></div></td></tr></table><div><br/></div><div Revisions to previous estimates added </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">6.5</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> MMBoe net PUD reserves and consisted of 21.4 MMBoe of upward revisions partially related to well performance revisions to reflect higher gas and NGL yields on older wells, which in turn increased total estimated ultimate recovery (&#8220;EURs&#8221;) for most of our PUD locations. These upward revisions were partially offset by 14.9 MMBoe of negative revisions for downward pricing adjustments (7.5 MMBoe) and PUD locations that were reclassified to unproven reserves due to: (i) such locations no longer being a part of our active development program, and (ii) 1.0 MMBoe removed for locations no longer expected to be developed within five years of their initial recording in accordance with SEC rules. All of our PUD locations are scheduled to be drilled within five years of their initial booking. Our PUD to proved developed reserves conversion rate was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">23%</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">For additional information and for a discussion of material changes on our total proved reserves, see </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">Supplemental Information About Oil &amp; Natural Gas Producing Activities</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data of this Annual Report. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:8px;padding-top:8px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Preparation of Reserve Estimates</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Our proved reserves are estimated by an independent engineering firm, Netherland, Sewell &amp; Associates, Inc. (&#8220;NSAI&#8221;). Reserve estimates are prepared in accordance with the definitions and regulations of the SEC and the Financial Accounting Standards Board (the &#8220;FASB&#8221;) using a deterministic method, which includes decline curve analysis, production performance analysis, offset analogies, and in some cases a combination of these methodologies.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Controls over Reserve Estimation</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">We maintain adequate and effective internal controls over the reserve estimation process and the underlying data which the reserve estimates are based upon. Our reserves estimation process is coordinated by our internal reserves department, which consists of qualified petroleum engineers, and is overseen by our Vice President of Reservoir Engineering. Reserve information, including models and other technical data, are stored on a secured database on our network. Certain non-technical inputs used in the reserves estimation process such as ownership interest percentages, oil and natural gas production, commodity prices, price differentials, operating and development costs and plug and abandonment estimates are obtained by other departments and are subject to our internal control process.&#160;Annually, our internal reserves department prepares a preliminary reserve database and meets with NSAI to discuss the assumptions and methods to be used in the year-end proved reserve estimation process and to review field performance and our future development plans. Following this review, the reserve database and supporting data is furnished to NSAI for their independent estimates and final report. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Qualifications of Responsible Technical Persons </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Our Vice President of Reservoir Engineering, Jeff Thompson, is responsible for overseeing the preparation of the reserves estimates. Mr. Thompson has held this position at Centennial since July 2017 and has over 10 years of relevant experience in reservoir engineering and reserve estimation. He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in petroleum engineering from the University of Oklahoma and is a Registered Professional Engineer in Oklahoma and member of the Society of Petroleum Engineers. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">NSAI was founded in 1961 and performs consulting petroleum engineering services under Texas Board of Professional Engineers Registration No. F-2699. Within NSAI, the technical persons primarily responsible for preparing the estimates set forth in the NSAI reserve report incorporated herein are Mr. Neil H. Little and Mr. Mike K. Norton. Mr. Little, a Licensed Professional Engineer in the State of Texas (No. 117966), has been practicing petroleum engineering at NSAI since 2011&#160;and has over 9 years </span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">12</span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;" href="#s7A24416E6E325981B2DB78D6BBC49653"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</span></a></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">of prior industry experience.
